questions.q:
The pH of a solution obtained by mixing 50 mL of 1 M HCl and 30 mL of 1 M NaOH is x×10-4. The value of x is (Nearest integer)
log 2.5=0.3979
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Milli equivalents of HClNaVa=50×1=50
Milli equivalents of NaOHNbVb=30×1=30
Since NaVa>NbVb
H+=NaVa-NbVbVa+Vb=50-3080=2080=0.25=2.5×10-1
pH=-logH+=-log2.5×10-1=1-0.3979=0.6021
pH×104=0.6021×104=6021

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The solubility product constant is the equilibrium constant for the dissolution of a solid substance into an aqueous solution. It is denoted by the symbol Ksp.

Solubility of CaF2=S mole//L

S=2.34×10-30.1×78=2.3478×10-2=3×10-4 mol/L

KspCaF2=4 S3=43×10-43

=108×10-12

=0.0108×10-8mol/L3

questions.q:
A litre of buffer solution contains 0.1 mole of each of NH3 and NH4Cl. On the addition of 0.02 mole of HCl by dissolving gaseous HCl, the pH of the solution is found to be _____×10-3 (Nearest integer)

Given: pKbNH3=4.745

log 2=0.301

log 3=0.477

T=298 K]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In resultant solution after addition of HCl to the basic buffer:

nNH3=0.1-0.02=0.08

nNH4Cl=nNH4+=0.1+0.02=0.12

Using Henderson-Hasselbach equation:

pOH=pKb+logNH4+NH3

=4.745+log0.120.08

=4.745+log32

=4.745+0.477-0.301

pOH=4.921
We know,

pH=14-pH

=9.079

questions.q:
If 1 mM solution of ethylamine produces $\mathrm{pH}=9$, then the ionization constant $\left(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}\right)$ of ethylamine is $10^{-x}$. The value of $x$ is ______ (nearest integer).
[The degree of ionization of ethylamine can be neglected with respect to unity.]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Given, $\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{H}}=9 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{OH}}=5 \Rightarrow[\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{OH}}]=10^{-5} \mathrm{M}$ Now, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_3^{+}\right][\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{H}]}{\left[\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_2\right]}\Rightarrow K_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{10^{-5} \times 10^{-5}}{10^{-3}}=10^{-7}$

questions.q:
The solubility product of BaSO4 is 1×10-10 at 298 K. The solubility of BaSO4 in 0.1M K2SO4(aq) solution is    ------×10-9 g L-1(nearest integer).
Given: Molar mass of BaSO4 is 233 g mol-1
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For the insoluble salt barium sulphate, sulphate ion added is the common ion. Due to the common ion effect the solubility of barium sulphate decreases. Let us assume solubility of barium sulphate is S.

BaSO4s⇌Ba2+Saq+SO42-S+0.1aq
 K2SO40.1-0.1⟶ K+0.1aq+SO42-0.1aq
KSP=Ba2+SO42-
1×10-10=S(S+0.1)
≃0.1 S
S=10-9M=233×10-9gL-1

questions.q:
Millimoles of calcium hydroxyide required to produce 100mL of the aqueous solution of pH 12 is x×10-1. The value of x is _____ (Nearest integer).
Assume complete dissociation.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
We know,
pH = -log[H+] , pH = -log[OH-], pH + pOH = 14
∵  pH=12

∴   H+=10-12M

∴   OH-=10-2M
We also know,
Ca(OH)2 ⇌ 2OH- + Ca2+

∴ Ca(OH)2=5×10-3M

5×10-3=milli moles of CaOH2 100mL

milli moles of CaOH2=5×10-1

Ans. =5

questions.q:
The titration curve of weak acid vs. strong base with phenolphthalein as indicator is shown below. The Kphenolphthalein =4×10-10

Given: log 2 = 0.3

The number of following statement/s which is/are correct about phenolphthalein is _______

A. It can be used as an indicator for the titration of weak acid with weak base.

B. It begins to change colour at pH = 8.4

C. It is a weak organic base

D. It is colourless in acidic medium
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Phenolphthalein is an organic acid and can be represented as HPh.

HPh (colourless) ⇌H++Ph- (Pink) 

Using Henderson equation for phenolphthalein

pH=pKIn+logPh-[HPh]

At equivalence point Ph-=[HPh]

∴pH2=pKIn=-log[4]+10=-0.6+10=9.4

Hence at (9.4±1)PH , phenolphthalein starts changing colour. Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic medium and pink in basic medium. Phenolphthalein indicator distinguish the pH change between 8 to 10. Therefore, it is used for strong acid and strong base titration or weak acid and strong base titration. Hence, A and C are incorrect statements.

!

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given:

Volume of Ba(NO3)2 solution = 25.0mL  Concentration of Ba(NO3)2 solution = 0.050M Volume of NaF solution = 25.0 mL  Concentration of NaF solution = 0.020M

Ba+2=25×0.0550=0.025M

F-=25×0.0250=0.01M

Ba+2 F-=25×10-7

Ksp=0.5×10-6=5×10-7

Ratio=Ba+2F-Ksp=25×10-75×10-7=5

questions.q:
600mL of 0.01M HCl is mixed with 400mL of 0.01M H2SO4. The pH of the mixture is _____×10-2. (Nearest integer)

[Given log2=0.30,   log3=0.48,  log5=0.69,   log7=0.84,   log11=1.04]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The number of millimoles = Molarity ×  Volume in mL

HCl produce one and H2SO4 produce two H+ ions respectively.

Total milimoles of H+=600×0.01+400×0.01×2=14
Thus, moles of hydrogen ion:
⇒H+=141000=14×10-3
⇒pH = -log[H+]=-log[14 × 10-3]

⇒pH=3-log14

=1.86

=186×10-2

Its solubility in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> solution is ___ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> (Round off to the Nearest integer) (Assume that solubility is much less than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In pure water,

Ksp=S2=8×10-42

=64×10-8

In 0.01 M H2SO4

H2SO4(aq)x→2H(aq)+x+SO42-(aq.)(x+0.01)

Ksp=x(x+0.01)

=64×10-8

x+0.01≅0.01 M

So, x(0.01)=64×10-8

x=64×10-6M

questions.subject: Chemistry

H2SO3 [Dibasic acid]

c=0.588 M

⇒ pH of solution is due to First dissociation only since Ka1>>Ka2

⇒ First dissociation of H2SO3

H2SO3(aq)⇌H⊕(aq)+HSO3-(aq) : ka1=1.7×10-2

t=      0

t       C-x              x                x

⇒1.7100=x20.588-x

⇒1.7×0.588-1.7x=100x2

⇒100x2+1.7x-1=0

⇒H⊕=x=-1.7+(1.7)2+4×100×12×100=0.09186
